body:
Fixes #29

## Summary

Issue #29 asks for a deep case study of parallel.ai, a complete list of requirements with solution plans, and a dependency-ordered set of issues for both `web-search` (search) and `web-capture` (fetching). This PR is documentation-only.

- `docs/case-studies/issue-29/README.md`: scope checklist, the six requirements of the issue with alternatives and selected plans, a verified inventory of every parallel.ai product (Search, Image Search, Extract, Task, Responses, Chat, FindAll, Entity Search, Monitor, Memory, webhooks, source policy, integrations, crawler) with inputs, outputs, latency, pricing, quotas and the local doc file for each claim, the current capability map of both repositories, a gap analysis that assigns each feature to a repository and a draft issue, per-feature solution alternatives with candidate libraries for JS and Rust, a mermaid dependency graph, a phased delivery order, and assumptions.
- `docs/case-studies/issue-29/issues/`: 26 ready-to-file issue drafts (`web-search-01…18`, `web-capture-01…08`), each with front matter (`id`, `repo`, `title`, `depends_on`, `labels`), summary, scope, acceptance criteria, and references.
- `docs/case-studies/issue-29/data/`: issue #29 and comments, issue lists of both repositories, the web-capture README, and the full public parallel.ai documentation snapshot (111 pages, OpenAPI 3.1 spec, `llms.txt`, agent skill) downloaded on 2026-10-07.
- `experiments/issue-29/download-parallel-docs.sh`: reproducible download of the snapshot.
- `experiments/issue-29/file-issues.sh`: files the drafts with `gh issue create` and links dependencies; it is a dry run unless `--apply` is passed.

## Issues were drafted, not filed

Creating 26 issues across two repositories is an outward-facing action, so the drafts are left for a maintainer to review and file with one command:

```bash
bash experiments/issue-29/file-issues.sh --apply
```

## Validation

- Download finished with `downloaded=111 failed=0`; the OpenAPI spec parses (37 operations, 183 schemas).
- A script checked that all 26 drafts reference only known ids and that the dependency graph is acyclic.
- The filing script dry run lists all 26 drafts and their dependencies without creating anything.
- Prettier passes on the new markdown; `data/` is excluded by `.prettierignore`.
- No code changes, so no changeset or Rust changelog fragment is needed.
